title: System Design in the AI Era
content: System design is often thought of as complex diagrams, databases, servers, APIs, load balancers, and difficult software engineering interviews. However, it is fundamentally one question: how to turn an idea into a real-world system. With the integration of AI agents, large language models, vector databases, and external services, system design has become even more crucial. Building a reliable product around an AI model is challenging, as calling an AI model is straightforward. This series will explore these aspects. The series will explain how modern software systems work, covering traditional topics such as APIs, databases, caching, and queues.
raw_text: When people hear the word system design, they usually imagine huge diagrams, databases, servers, APIs, load balancers, and maybe a very difficult software engineering interview. But system design is actually much simpler than that. It is basically one question. How do we take an idea and turn it into a system that actually works in the real world? And now that we are building the applications with AI agents, large language models, vector databases, tools and external services, system design is becoming even more important. Because calling an AI model is easy, building a reliable product around that model is the difficult part. And that's exactly what we are going to explore in this series.
